Raw Client Material:

Discovery call notes, 6 October 2026 (fictional). Attendees: Dana Whitfield,
General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional); Ravi Okafor, CISO; Ingrid
Solberg, Head of Quality.

- Tamarack designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. HQ in
  the Netherlands; plants in the Netherlands and Germany; sales office in the
  United States. About 1,100 staff; Dana said revenue is "in the US$200 to
  300 million range".
- AI today: a customer service chatbot on the support portal is live
  (deployed). An AI visual inspection system on the German production line is
  in pilot. They plan to use AI for sales forecasting next year.
- Dana: "We are piloting, not scaling. I want governance in place before
  visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
- Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS; Ingrid runs the quality management
  system under ISO 9001. They would like to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next
  year.
- Dana named the EU AI Act and the GDPR as the rules they are watching.
- Internal audit reported in June 2026 that there is no inventory of AI
  systems.
- Constraints: budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year; customer
  data must stay in the EU; the German works council must be consulted before
  anything touches production staff.
- Who would attend: Dana, Ravi, Ingrid, the Head of Data (Tomas Reyes), the
  German plant manager and two internal auditors.
- Dana is the budget holder for this. Decision expected by 15 December 2026.

A statement of a Client fact that Part 2 of the fixture does not contain (incumbent 'internal audit function' beyond the framework names; the Part 2 block is not shown, so this is likely but not certain)
judgment_calls: Whether '(Ravi Okafor)' means source or owner is ambiguous. Beside '(Ingrid Solberg)', who is stated to run the QMS, it reads as an owner attribution. Another scorer could read it as a speaker citation and pass it.

Part 2 of the fixture was not provided. I assumed it lists only the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 QMS as incumbent frameworks. If it includes internal audit, that part of the failure falls away.

The v1.14.3 guidance treats unstated incumbent functions and owner attributions as failures, so I applied it. Without that guidance, a scorer reading item 3 only as 'traceable to the notes' might pass this response.
'support portal' is quoted as client terminology under Rule 5. I treated that as harmless and not a fact problem.
score.reasoning: Format, field completeness and halt logic are correct. The case fails on traceability. The INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS field attributes the ISMS to Ravi Okafor, an ownership relation the notes do not state, and it adds an 'internal audit function' as an incumbent function. Under the scorer guidance, both are unstated owners or functions, so checklist item 3 is not met. The other elements pass, but partial compliance is a FAIL.
